아버지.forms: 아버지가 · 아버지를 · honorific: 아버님 · casual: 아빠
아버지.x: My father works at a bank.
아버지.e: Casual form 아빠 (dad); add 할 and get 할아버지 (grandfather).
아버지.t: Use honorific verbs for parents: 아버지께서 주무세요 (Father is sleeping).

수요일.x: I'm meeting a friend on Wednesday evening.
수요일.e: 'Water day' — named for Mercury, the water planet.

산.x: I went to the mountains with friends on the weekend.
산.e: Mountain names end in -산, like 남산. Hiking is a national pastime.

아파트.x: I live on the tenth floor of an apartment building.
아파트.e: From English 'apartment', but it means a high-rise apartment complex — where most Koreans live.
아파트.t: Small units are 원룸 or 빌라.

빠르다.x: The subway is faster than the bus.
빠르다.e: 빨리 = quickly — think of Korea's famous 빨리빨리 ('hurry hurry') culture.
빠르다.t: 르 irregular: 르 + 아요 becomes 라요 with an extra ㄹ — 빠르다 → 빨라요.

진하다.m: to be strong, to be thick (of drinks, flavors); to be dark, deep (of colors)
진하다.x: I drink strong coffee every morning.
진하다.e: Think of a thick, concentrated liquid — the opposite of watery.
진하다.t: Strong coffee is 진한 커피, not 강한 커피; light coffee or pale colors are 연하다.

계좌 번호.ex: 계좌 번호 알려 주시면 바로 보내 드릴게요.
계좌 번호.x: If you tell me your account number, I'll send it right away.
계좌 번호.t: Always give the bank name with it: 은행 이름하고 계좌 번호. The digits are read one by one with Sino-Korean numbers.

스타일.ex: 그 사람은 옷 스타일이 정말 멋있어요.
스타일.x: That person's clothing style is really cool.
스타일.t: 제 스타일이에요 can mean 'He's (or she's) my type,' not just 'my style.'

늘리다.m: to increase, to expand, to extend
늘리다.x: The company increased its number of employees this year.
늘리다.e: Causative of 늘다 'to grow, to increase': to make something grow.
늘리다.t: Don't confuse it with 늘이다, which means to physically stretch something longer.

끊어지다.m: to be cut off, to be disconnected; to snap, to break (a string)
끊어지다.x: The call suddenly got cut off while we were talking.
끊어지다.e: From 끊다 (to cut, to hang up) + -어지다 (to become).
끊어지다.t: Pronounced [끄너지다] — the ㅎ in ㄶ is silent.

적극.x: I strongly agree with that opinion.
적극.e: Literally 'piled up to the extreme' — full effort.
적극.t: Usually used right before a verb: 적극 지원하다 'to actively support', 적극 추천하다 'to highly recommend'.

다리미.x: The day before the interview, I ironed my shirt.
다리미.e: Built from 다리다 'to iron clothes'; don't confuse with 다리 'leg' or 'bridge'.

엄하다.ex: 우리 아버지는 어릴 때 아주 엄하셨어요.
엄하다.x: My father was very strict when I was young.

부가세.t: Pronounced [부가쎄]. In Korea it's 10% and usually already in the menu price.

대변인.ex: 정부 대변인은 오늘 오후 기자 회견을 열었습니다.
대변인.x: The government spokesperson held a press conference this afternoon.
대변인.e: Literally 'a person who speaks on someone's behalf.'

수면제.x: Please take sleeping pills only after talking with a doctor.

망원경.x: Looking at the moon through a telescope was really amazing.

외교관.ex: 제 꿈은 외교관이 되어서 해외에서 일하는 거예요.
외교관.x: My dream is to become a diplomat and work abroad.
외교관.e: Literally 'outside-exchange official': an official who handles dealings with other countries.

친근감.ex: 그 배우는 이웃집 사람처럼 친근감이 느껴져요.
친근감.x: That actor feels as familiar as the person next door.

후하다.ex: 그 식당은 인심이 후해서 손님이 많아요.
후하다.x: That restaurant is generous with its portions, so it has lots of customers.
후하다.e: Literally 'thick' — generosity pictured as an ample, thick portion.
후하다.t: Common collocations: 인심이 후하다 and 점수를 후하게 주다 (to grade generously).

어수선하다.m: messy, cluttered; unsettled, chaotic (of a mood or situation)
어수선하다.ex: 이사 중이라 집 안이 좀 어수선해요.
어수선하다.x: We're in the middle of moving, so the house is a bit of a mess.
어수선하다.t: Also for moods and society: 분위기가 어수선하다 'the atmosphere is unsettled.'

콘텐츠.ex: 그 회사는 어린이를 위한 교육 콘텐츠를 만들어요.
콘텐츠.x: That company makes educational content for children.
콘텐츠.e: From English 'contents' — Korean keeps the plural s, even for a single piece of content.

특수성.ex: 정책을 만들 때 지역의 특수성을 고려해야 해요.
특수성.x: When making policy, you have to consider each region's particular circumstances.

극지방.ex: 극지방의 얼음이 줄면서 해수면이 높아지고 있습니다.
극지방.x: Sea levels are rising as the ice in the polar regions shrinks.
극지방.t: Pronounced [극찌방] — the ㅈ is tensed after ㄱ.

맥박.x: The nurse is taking the patient's pulse.
맥박.t: Use 재다 with it: 맥박을 재다 (take a pulse); 맥박이 빠르다 means a fast pulse.

가슴이 찢어지다.forms: 가슴이 찢어져요 · 가슴이 찢어질 것 같아요
가슴이 찢어지다.m: to be heartbroken, to be torn apart with grief or pity (lit. the chest tears apart)
가슴이 찢어지다.ex: 아파하는 아이를 보니까 가슴이 찢어질 것 같아요.
가슴이 찢어지다.x: Seeing my child in pain breaks my heart.
가슴이 찢어지다.e: Grief or pity so strong that the chest feels as if it were being ripped (찢어지다 'to tear').
가슴이 찢어지다.t: Strong and emotional, often with -(으)ㄹ 것 같다; used for one's own loss or for deep pity at someone else's suffering.

공론장.m: public sphere, forum for public debate
공론장.ex: 인터넷은 새로운 공론장의 역할을 하고 있습니다.
공론장.x: The internet is playing the role of a new public sphere.
공론장.e: Literally 'place for public discussion'; translates Habermas's 'public sphere'.

지방정부.ex: 지방정부와 중앙정부가 협력해서 문제를 해결해야 해요.
지방정부.x: Local and central governments need to work together to solve the problem.

카타르시스.ex: 슬픈 영화를 보고 나면 카타르시스를 느껴요.
카타르시스.x: I feel a sense of catharsis after watching a sad movie.

집약하다.m: to condense, to summarize, to concentrate
집약하다.ex: 이 보고서는 연구 결과를 한 장으로 집약했어요.
집약하다.x: This report condensed the research findings into one page.

내부고발자.x: Thanks to a whistleblower, the company's corruption came to light.
내부고발자.e: Literally 'inside-reporting person'; the official legal term is 공익신고자.

옥석구분.m: good and bad perishing together, indiscriminate destruction
옥석구분.ex: 무리한 단속은 옥석구분의 결과를 낳을 수 있습니다.
옥석구분.x: Heavy-handed crackdowns can end up harming the innocent along with the guilty.
옥석구분.e: Literally 'jade and stone burn together' — fire doesn't care which is precious.
옥석구분.t: Often misused as if 구분 meant 'distinguish'; for sorting good from bad, say 옥석을 가리다 instead.
rel: jade and stone, the good and the bad

기축통화.ex: 달러는 세계의 기축통화 역할을 하고 있습니다.
기축통화.x: The dollar serves as the world's key currency.
기축통화.e: Literally 'currency that is the base axis' of world trade.

중추신경.ex: 우리 몸의 뇌와 척수는 중추신경에 속합니다.
중추신경.x: The brain and spinal cord in our body belong to the central nervous system.
